text:
lee_wilson: Heads-up — after the checkpoint onboard yesterday staging p99 token latency doubled on long prompts (~1.5k tokens). Seeing it on the canary too. :eyeglasses:

maria_garcia: ugh, saw alerts. Is this the quantized variant rollout?

ashley: canary trace shows kernel fallback for attention on a lot of requests: falls back to `gemm_fallback` path at ~3rd block. p50 ok, p95/p99 spike.

jonathan: logs attached in infra: `kernel_selector: fallback=true reason="layout-mismatch"` a ton of those. Might be tokenizer length distribution change triggering different block sizes.

lee_wilson: I ran a quick profile. nvprof shows hot on slower kernel with much higher memory copies. snippet:
```
# top 2 frames (simplified)
1  42.3%  aten::matmul_slow_path
2  18.7%  copy_async_kernel
```

maria_garcia: hmm tokenizer change in the new checkpoint added a couple of special tokens; sequence chunking changed. That can change block alignments and kernel selection thresholds.

jonathan: I bisected canary -> staging. Reproducer: `seq_len=1536 batch=1 model=v2-checkpoint-2026-03 quant=4bit` When I pin old tokenizer map the fallback disappears. Bisect points to onboarding PR 3246 (tokenizer mapping + config tweak).

ashley: CI perf test failed but was borderline (10% p99 variance) so it got merged. We need to stop the rollout until we have a fix. Can we canary-revert? @deploy-bot canary status?

deploy-bot: @eng-runtime Canary rollout: 40% -> paused (manual) after alert. Current canary batch pinned to 3 instances. Revert request: queued.

lee_wilson: I'm trying a runtime patch that relaxes the strict layout mismatch and forces re-evaluation of kernel heuristics (cheap check) to avoid fallback when quantization layout is identical in practice. Patch branch: `runtime/fuzzy-kernel-match-2026-03`.

perf-bot: perf job started: `jenkins/job/eng-runtime/pipeline/7891` — running microbenchmarks with offending checkpoint and old tokenizer map.

maria_garcia: short-term mitigation: pin tokenizer mapping for canary to old map and force model variant `v2-checkpoint-2026-02` for production traffic routing. That should restore latency while we root cause.

jonathan: For the bisect notes — root cause looks like two things: tokenizer changed tokenization patterns (padding + BOS placement) which shifts sequence chunk borders; AND the kernel selector has a tight threshold where a single token shift flips to a slower fallback kernel. I'll open an RFC to make kernel selection resilient to +/-1 token shifts and add a warmup step in onboarding to collect chunk distribution.

ashley: Actions:
- maria: pin tokenizer map on canary & staging rollback (in progress)
- lee: land fuzzy-kernel-match hotfix + perf run -> if good, ship canary patch
- jonathan: RFC for selector heuristics + onboarding warmup test
- ashley: stop any further checkpoint onboardings until we confirm fix

lee_wilson: quick note — temporary RPC knob `runtime.kernel.strict_layout=false` added to prod feature flags so we can flip without deploy if needed.

maria_garcia: thanks. I'll also add a CI test case for tokenization chunk distribution differences to catch this earlier.

jonathan: closing loop: if perf job passes with hotfix I'll request canary resume with 5% traffic for 2 hours then ramp. If it fails we'll revert the onboard completely.

lee_wilson: updating the incident doc with links to bisect, logs, and the profiling dump. ping me if you need pair debugging. :thumbsup:
